blocks.text: To begin with the name: it should be known that, like the Hebrew צב, the Arabic ضب [ḍabb] is written with the same letters. But, as the dialects vary, the Arabic Tsade at the beginning of a word is pronounced as d or dh, because of the dot added to it. Thus this little word is pronounced ضب [ḍabb] dhab among the Arabs. The plural is ضباب [ḍibāb] dhibab, or أضب [aḍubb] adhab, and the feminine ضبة [ḍabba] dhabba. Hence ضبب [ḍabab] dhabab, and مضب [maḍabb] mudhab, and مضبب [muḍbib] mudhbib denote a place full of these animals; and مضبب [muḍabbib] mudhabbib their hunter. Further, ضب [ḍabb] dhab is defined by Damir as حيوان بري معروف من الحشرات يشبه الورل [ḥayawān barrī maʿrūf min al-ḥasharāt yushbih al-waral] a well-known wild animal among the reptiles, similar to the guaril, or greater stellio: just as Avicenna writes that it differs from the guaril, وان كان [wa-in kāna] [II, 465] يشبهه وكان قريب الاحوال والقوي منه [yushbihuhu wa-kāna qarīb al-aḥwāl wa-al-quwā minhu] although it is similar to it, and very close to it both in constitution and in powers. So he writes in the second book of the Canon, in the chapter ضب [ḍabb] dhab, or tsab, if you prefer. And in the chapter حردون [ḥardūn] chardaun, [col. 1046] which was entirely omitted by the Latin translator: هو الضب وطبعه قريب من طبع الورل وهو اشبه الوزغ بما يتعزي به [huwa al-ḍabb wa-ṭabʿuhu qarīb min ṭabʿ al-waral wa-huwa ashbah al-wazagh bi-mā yataʿazzī bihi] Chardaun is the same as dhab: its nature comes close to the guaril, and its attributes are the same as those of the guezga. And in the chapter ورل [waral] guaril, هو غير الضب والضب لا يكون او قل ما يكون الا في البادية وراسه وبدنه وذنبه خالف من الورل وربما قريب في طبايعه [huwa ghayr al-ḍabb wa-al-ḍabb lā yakūn aw qalla mā yakūn illā fī al-bādiya wa-raʾsuhu wa-badanuhu wa-dhanabuhu khālif min al-waral wa-rubbamā qarīb fī ṭabāyiʿihi] The guaril is different from the dhab. For the dhab is not found, or only rarely, anywhere but in the desert. And it differs from the guaril in head, trunk and tail, although it is close to it in nature. And Abdollatif of Baghdad: الورل والضب والحربا وشحمة الارض والوزغ كلها متناسبة في الخلق [al-waral wa-al-ḍabb wa-al-ḥirbā wa-shaḥmat al-arḍ wa-al-wazagh kulluhā mutanāsiba fī al-khalq] The guaril, and the dhab, and the hirba, and the fat of the earth, and the guezga all share the same nature. These, namely, are so many species of lizards, of which we shall speak below. Therefore ضب [ḍabb] dhab, or צב tsab, which is the same, is neither a toad, nor a bramble-toad, nor a tortoise, nor a shelled animal, but belongs to the lizard kind. Now, so that it may be known more fully, we shall say what the Critics, Philosophers, Theologians, Magicians and Physicians of the Arabs have written about it, most of which has not yet been published.

The Critics, then, teach that it is an animal πολυώνυμον [polyōnymon], with many names. For besides ضب [ḍabb] dhab, or צב tsab, the common name, it is also called حردون [ḥardūn] chardaun (the Chaldeans write חרדונא chara[?], the Syrians ܚܕܪܘܢܐ chadrona, and the Samaritans [?] adrona, as will be shown below). It is likewise called برق [barq] bork, and علين [ʿlyn] alin, and هيقل [hayqal] haikal. And, if it is fat, سبحل [?] or سحبل [siḥbal] sichbal: if old, قرسم [qirsim] kirsem; if of bad disposition, ضغطار [ḍighṭār] dhiphtar: just as the female is commonly ضبة [ḍabba] dhabba; but, when fat, حيكانا [ḥaykānā] chaicana; when with young, مكون [makūn] machun, and ممكن [mumkin] mamchin. From the verb مكن [makina] machina, proper to this animal and to the locust when they lay eggs, the egg is مكين [makīn] machin, and شلقة [shalqa] silka. The young in general, حضرم [ḥiḍrim] chidhrim; the first, مطبح [muṭbiḥ] mutbich; when just hatched from the egg, حسل [ḥisl] chisel; when already more grown, غيداق [ghaydāq] chaidak. The fat which it has around the belly and the root of the tail, كشية [kushya] chusia. And حلم [ḥalama] halama properly means to take out that fat, just as عكد [ʿakida] achada, to be fat, is used of the dhab ضب [ḍabb] alone. The male member, in the dual, نزكان [nazkān] nazachani; because it is forked. Hence the animal itself is also called سديم [sadīm] sadim, that is, [II, 466] well furnished in that part. Its hiding-place is عكدة [ʿukda] ochda, and عرن [ʿirn] arin, and [col. 1047] لغز [lughz] logoz, but more commonly جحر [juḥr] giochar, whence جحر الضب [jaḥara al-ḍabb] the dhab has entered its hiding-place. And اجحر فلان [ajḥara fulān] someone drove it into its hiding-place. But ادلق [adlaqa] adlaka he poured water into it, so that the dhab would come out. And دلق الضب [dalaqa al-ḍabb] dalaka dhab, that is, it came out of its hiding-place because of the water poured in. And اهوي يده الي الضب [ahwā yadahu ilā al-ḍabb] he put in his hand to catch the dhab. And حرش [ḥarasha] charasa, he hunted, used properly of this animal. These things have been gathered and excerpted here and there from Giauhari, Alcamus and other books of the Critics.
